reviews.text: This is a film obsessed both by its characters’ personal histories, and by its own. But it really soars when it is smartly combining the old with the new.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: While it’s overall a bumpy ride; “No Time to Die” is definitely a great Bond film, and the perfect swansong for Daniel Craig.
reviews.author: Paul Emmanuel Enicola

reviews.text: If you watch Bond movies to learn more about Bond than saving the world, then you may be pleased to know that it ties up a lot of loose ends for the character without sacrificing what we enjoy about the character.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Whatever you think of Daniel Craig or his wrist-slashing attitude to 007, it can’t be denied that he has forever changed the franchise and ensured the future for James Bond looks very bright indeed.
reviews.author: Daryl MacDonald

reviews.text: Bond films are generally entertaining and this one is no exception. It’s just not exceptional.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Everything you wanted! It’s Dr No meets Skyfall! Fukunaga crafted the most pure James Bond experience yet! Bringing a perfect, emotional, & VISCERAL send off for Daniel Craig. The action is insane, the score is PERFECTION, & such a smooth runtime!
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: The overall tone of the film is somber as time is brought up as a major theme to remind audiences their time with Craig is coming to a close.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Bond sequels have always recycled elements from its predecessors. But No Time to Die, the 25th film in the franchise, reaches back half a century to borrow almost exclusively from On Her Majesty’s Secret Service.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: No Time To Die is the most emotional, personal James Bond movie of Daniel Craig's Era, holding a heartfelt farewell to the now-iconic actor. Massive praise to the outstanding ensemble cast.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Add in a stellar performance from Daniel Craig, gorgeous cinematography from Director of Photography Linus Sandgren, and great direction from Cory Joji Fukunaga, and it’s one of the year’s best and an all-time Bond film.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: It's filled with a spectacularly grand "this is the end" feeling and heartfelt drama that is unquestionably earned after all of these years.
reviews.author: Alex Billington

reviews.text: No Time to Die is an amalgam of all that has been the Craig Bond experience. The thrills are all still there and the action segments are among the best the franchise has offered.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: The 25th installment of the long-running spy series: James Bond film franchise. The blockbuster film's plot opened with a prologue explaining how Agent 007 James Bond's (Daniel Craig in his last outing as MI6 agent) former partner and psychotherapist
reviews.author: Tim Dirks

reviews.text: The action scenes aren’t particularly memorable like the parkour scene in Casino Royale. There’s no weighty grief in the way Bond nurses a broken heart in Quantum of Solace, and surely none of the bitterness or existential dread from Skyfall.
reviews.author: Tatsam Mukherjee

reviews.text: No Time to Die is just this bloated, lumbering thing that is bogged down by the weight of what came before and it just ponders along until it collapses.
reviews.author: Vera Wylde

reviews.text: Directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga, “No Time to Die” comes packaged with everything you want from a Bond movie – big action, even bigger characters, plenty of style, and a special dash of heart.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Franchise familiarity bubbles away in the film's veins, expectedly, but Fukunaga knows what to shake, stir, change and challenge, and what makes a moving, ambitious and entertaining farewell.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: ... A dark and assured piece of filmmaking, enjoyable from start to finish.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: Sometimes overexplains, and at times the script is condescending... though it leaves you satisfied in the end. Good fan service. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Not the perfect send-off, but enough brilliant set-pieces.
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Fukunaga nurtures Bond’s emotional journey — such as it is; he’s not a master of brutality like John Wick, but neither is he Anne of Green Gables — down the home stretch.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The film leaves one with a bittersweet farewell to the legacy that Craig has cemented while also maintaining a sense of optimism for what the future may hold.
reviews.author: Josh Parham

reviews.text: All in all, No Time To Die is as Bond as you can get with action and car chases aplenty, witty dialogue and jokes to be had, but most of all, it is a befitting send-off to Craig’s iconic rendition of the much loved MI6 agent.
reviews.author: Britany Murphy

reviews.text: As Bond villains go, Safin checks off a lot of boxes: a scheme with globally catastrophic implications? An island hideout? A weird name ("Lyutsifer")? It's just too bad Malek manages to be even less menacing than Dominic Greene.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Fukanaga delivers a good-looking movie with a couple of fine action sequences, but No Time to Die doesn't dazzle.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: NO TIME TO DIE is a visually stunning, emotional showdown of the Daniel Craig era. Cary Joji Fukunagas film has the usual 007 ingredients, but still goes a step further and serves us a Bond that we have never experienced before.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: Craig comes back to the role of Bond in full form, while Waltz and Malek both deliver the goods in terms of creepy Bond villainy.  Ana De Armas damn near steals the movie.
reviews.author: David Reddish

reviews.text: What keeps this bulky ship afloat? A sturdy star turn from Craig, for one.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: An excellent achievement.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: A fitting send-off for Craig. Hes the man who dragged 007 into the 21st Century with an edgier look, and he finishes his tenure with a lot of heart. There will be many James Bonds to come, but few will do it this well.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: "'No Time To Die' is a Bond movie thats got air in its lungs, but struggles to stay in tune with itself. Theres too much slack in its dramatic stakes."
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: As familiar faces including Moneypenny, M and Q are reintroduced James Bond gets better. There is a real sense of humanity that cuts through all those old character traits, to reveal a genuine emotional core.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: Sure the film might not be the revelation some were hoping for and is far from being the best Bond film even just within the Craig era, but the film still survives as a fitting and moving goodbye for Craig marking the end of an era.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: No Time to Die is utterly cinematic. It's strong storytelling with big action set pieces that will leave you breathless...No Time to Die sets its sights on giving Craig's Bond era the goodbye it deserves.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: There is something to sitting and taking in the whole of Bonds machismo across No Time To Die, as it stretches and unfurls. You see the cracks Craig has worked to put in his foundation, his hardheadedness and fragility.
reviews.author: Zosha Millman

reviews.text: No Time to Die is an overlong and overwrought action thriller. The cinematography is often stunning, but the action sequences are exhausting.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: ... continues to raise the bar in terms of visual extravagance, even if this installment lacks the substance to match the spectacle.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: For the makers of these movies world domination is an ambition fulfilled a long time ago.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: No Time to Die doesn't hit the highs of Craig's best Bond outings, but takes some hard swings to challenge audience preconceptions of what the franchise can and can't do - and they mostly pay off.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: NO TIME TO DIE is a film that is worthy of Daniel Craig's excellent performance as James Bond. The series has moved on to a form that is more realistic, but still has exciting action sequences that are key to spy films.
reviews.author: Dolores Quintana

reviews.text: Even James Bond proved something of a dud in the final iteration of Daniel Craig's run as the British super spy.
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: Where "No Time to Die" succeeds is in the moments of Craig as Bond, a man reckoning with a career of death and destruction. What is all that sound and fury for?
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: It all goes downhill after that first explosive 20 minutes...large stretches are mopey and fussy.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Malek is the consummate character actor, and his portrayal of the villainous Safin is excellent.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: With No Time To Die, the 25th entry in the series as a whole and Craig's fifth and final outing, audiences say goodbye to Bond in a way that feels undoubtedly earned, triumphant, and bittersweet all at once.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: The latest James Bond outing may be uneven but it still offers plenty of excitement and fun.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: A big, ambitious, explosive endgame for Craig's fifteen-year tenure as Bond.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: Surprisingly, even with the sour notes of those effortful closing moments, there's so many more engaging things beyond Bond that I find myself feeling quite pleasant about the entire experience.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Even with familiar characters imperiled more effectively than in earlier installments, the stakes are virtually nonexistent. And a main character who exists in a vacuum is largely airless and empty.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: ...no action film can ingest a full hour without any action to speak of...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: What i can say with a certain amount of certainty is that this is definitely not the strongest of the Craig/Bond films.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: For the most part a very consistent Craig-tenure Bond installment with a boiler-plate Bond plot which for the most part delivers.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: I would happily watch it again but not if I was in the mood to watch a Bond film as No Time To Die does not scratch that particular itch...
reviews.author: David Hogan

reviews.text: The best one since Peter Hunt's On Her Majesty's Secret Service and for many of the same reasons.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: It was cool, it just didn't mean that much to me.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: Mr. Craig... thank you for your service. Mr. Bond... see you again soon.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: [Bond] constantly see-saws between wanting to be harshly realistic and an awareness that going silly is where the money is; fans of bionic eyes and post-murder quips will not leave disappointed
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: No Time To Die achieves every goal it sets itself, and does so with heart, grit, guts and the occasional wry smile.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: It is the characterisation in No Time to Die that does not simply save it, but makes it a genuinely satisfying film to watch.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: Tones down the villainy and action leaving room for Bond's humanity to evolve with a surprise or two before he gets his rather explosive send-off.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: No Time To Die gets the unfathomable task done: ending things definitively for this James Bond
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Even with the crummy villain, it was just such a pleasure to watch. Daniel Craig is just so good in this role. That's the fun of this big send off.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: 007's exploits are heightened, operatic, grand, and measured in emotion rather than that most useless of cinematic yardsticks, realism,
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: With his long upper lip and reluctance to crack a smile, [Daniel Craig] could have made his mark as the only grumpy Bond, but the pulsing intelligence behind the gloom has transformed it into gravitas without slowing down his performance.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: [No Time To Die uses] our comfort-food familiarity with underwater spy vehicles, villainous lairs and breathless, ticking-clock countdowns as distraction while an unlikely tenderness sneaks in to knock you sideways.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Whilst the film's pacing and execution is occasionally lacking, No Time To Die can't be faulted as the bombastic swan song it lovingly intends to be.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: One of the most successful elements of No Time to Die is how well it blends the seeming contradictions of the Bond films.
reviews.author: Thomas Caldwell

reviews.text: No Time To Die is, on balance, a kinetic, expansive and stirring capstone to Craig's adventures in those perfectly tailored Tom Ford suits.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Has one of the weakest villains and conspiracies in the history of the Bond saga. Rami Malek simply isn't a good enough actor to draw you into his character's psychopathology.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: What elevates this above a standard action movie is the direction of Cary Joji Fukunaga who infuses the film with memorable set pieces and a distinctive style.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: ...the right send-off for the man who has been 007 for a whole new generation.
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's no-BS Bond rocks steel-tipped purpose like a bespoke tux.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: The Daniel Craig 007 era comes to a merciful close with this punishingly overlong and predominantly ineffective entry that marks an obvious low point for the venerable series...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Do you know that awful feeling when you anticipate something (in this case, a film) for so long, only to end up with a bitter disappointment? Well, that's exactly how I felt after I watched No Time to Die.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: When you take a step back and look at No Time To Die's achievements as an individual Bond outing, it's a bit of a boring mess.
reviews.author: Alicia Gilstorf

reviews.text: One of the best, most satisfying Bonds yet...What makes No Time To Die a genuine step-up for the Bond franchise is that it actually has a great character story, one you can truly invest in.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: A terrific send off for Daniel Craig and his era. A huge, bombastic blockbuster of the best kind... Despite slightly muddled pacing in parts, it's easily the single best Craig-era bond, and perhaps my favourite ever!
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: A glorious grand finale. A whirlwind of emotions and great cinema that bids farewell to Daniel Craig's 007 as it deserves.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Mature Bond for a mature audience; the love story is heartily and admirably committed to.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: A powerful end to the Craig era, although probably not for the reasons that everyone would like.
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: Fukunaga confirmes his ability to handle different genres with solvency. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: The agent at a mature age, more romantic than seducer but also less witty.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: While it's not perfect, it's a thoroughly enjoyable send-off for Craig's final turn as 007.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: When the movie has a one track mind and cuts out the extra nonsense, there's a sweeping allure that encapsulates the final 30 minutes. But overall, it's a bloated experience.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: The new James Bond movie, No Time To Die, is so disappointing that I don't see how the iconic franchise can be reformed...
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: It's been a long wait, but they pulled it off -- Craig can retire in peace. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: No Time to Die's pieces are all there, but its execution is slightly underwhelming... When it works, it works. It's just not as good as it could have been, and that's slightly disappointing.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: Lashana Lynch is a total blast as the MI6 agent Nomi, both a worthy rival for Bond as well as a potential replacement.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: A very silly movie wrapped in serious clothes, saved single-handedly by Daniel Craig's raw, wounded performance.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: More indulgent and exhausting than entertaining.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: After 15 years and five films Daniel Craig has retired from the role that brought him international fame. Almost certainly unwittingly, Craig will also be associated with the demise of James Bond as we knew him.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: ... fails to live up to the potential of (Casino) Royale and Skyfall, undermining this Bond series-within-a-series; Craig nevertheless wrings every ounce of anger and angst out of the super spy, making his portrayal an impossible act to follow.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: [No Time To Die] begins inside a memory and ends with a kind of apocalypse. Sound familiar? Not really. Memory has never been a prominent theme in the series, and the mood of this instalment is different in many ways.
reviews.author: Michael Wood

reviews.text: And in a welcome surprise - assertive women show up in an impressive triumvirate of Ana de Armas, Lashana Lynch and Lea Seydoux.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: While the motivations, or at least the back stories, of some of the characters are less than clear, the story works well enough for an action film with a lot more heart and soul than is usual in this series.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: No Time to Die looks and feels like a Skyfall while playing like a Spectre-good and bad comingling in a way that's almost fitting.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: In the best Bond tradition... offers up implausibilities with shameless abandon, like a helpful bartender serving one martini after another, fully aware that each serving is dulling your critical thinking skills.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's Bonds are not a bad place to start with [the character]. His Bond feels real, relevant to this time and immediate.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: Fans will enjoy seeing Bond's non-stop hand-to-hand combat and his iconic driving skills--cinematography is stunning.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: The last with Daniel Craig in the lead, the film brings together the various aspects of his nonconformist interpretation of James Bond in a most satisfying way.
reviews.author: Namrata Joshi

reviews.text: The film's sole distinction is the fact that it's the James Bond epic that finally manages to make 007 a crashing bore.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: With this fifth and final go-round, it's clear who the best Bond is. It's Craig, Daniel Craig.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Absolutely faithful to the Bondian canon, Cary Jonji Fukunaga's film brings the series full circle. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: Too long, too complex script-wise, but still entertaining. It's Bond!
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: A decent farewell to Craig's Bond. It is a bit too lengthy. I wish there was more Ana de Armas, she was a standout.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Sophisticated entertainment, as well as poignant reflexion on bioweapons, fallible heroes, and love.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: Through it all, Craig's Bond rarely cracks a smile. He's no longer a secret agent. He's a mope. However, as the torpid tale progresses, he has to return to being a secret agent. But he will not stop being a mope.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's richly layered performance in No Time to Die just might attract Oscar's attention...
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: While it's certainly a suitable big splash for Daniel Craig's final portrayal as Bond, it's not quite as satisfying as some of his other offerings.
reviews.author: Gemma Creagh

reviews.text: Craig exits the franchise having earned a great deal of goodwill in the role despite a mixed record...he exits on a high note in No Time to Die, and that's more than you can say for Sean Connery in Never Say Never Again and Brosnan in Die Another Day...
reviews.author: Justin Charity

reviews.text: The "every other Craig Bond film is good" trend holds true and gives the star a worthy send-off.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: From the roaring sound of high-speed chases to the lush window dressing of breathtaking vistas and suave outfits, it's a blast to watch the series' controlled indulgence streak unfold.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: As a Bond movie it works. It's enjoyable... But it's not the Avengers Endgame of the Bond universe.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: [Craig's] become to Bond what Peter Capaldi was to Doctor Who: all brave promise of grit and innovation, finally swallowed whole by scripts that were both too maudlin and too silly.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: Overlong and with some weak (and confusing) spots, this outing still has a grand, tragic arc, with spectacular action and characters -- both James Bond and the others -- who feel more human.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Fukunaga does a pretty solid job within the formal restrictions of the long-running franchise, balancing blockbuster commercial necessity with more artful auteur touches.
reviews.author: Stephen Dalton

reviews.text: No Time to Die is an outstanding end to Daniel Craig's James Bond era.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: I can't say it's not necessarily the best, but it is the most ambitious and it succeeds in ways that should have Bond fans debating the results for some time to come.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: No Time to Die, the bombastic finale to Craig's run of James Bond flicks, is big, and proud to be big.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Craig's distinctive persona suggests pathos that the series doesn't allow; instead, he's merely used as a Bond-piñata, a straining for an element of realism amid stunts that, in their grandiosity and their excess, preclude it.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Rather than a propulsive, operatic, crescendo of a finale to Daniel Craig's tenure as Bond, a pretty shaggy, indulgent one.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A stage of evolution closes here, and it feels satisfying.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Whether or not Ian Fleming came to terms with his own mortality before he passed away is something we'll never know, but director Cary Fukunaga and the writers of No Time to Die gave his greatest creation the chance to make this final discovery.
reviews.author: Dave Schilling

reviews.text: The result is 2 hours and 48 minutes that veer into every possible mood, some more successful than others, but it is never a stale cocktail.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Director, co/screenplay writer Cary Joji Fukunaga knows what we come to see and how to delivers just that.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: It's sometimes thrilling, but even when it isn't, it satisfies.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: A sensational sendoff for Daniel Craig's James Bond.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: No Time to Die is just as dull and unimaginative as its title. It's yet another bloated, vapid and overproduced blockbuster that's more exhausting than fun or exhilarating.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: It's a bit overlong, trying to do everything it can to send Craig off in style, and while it doesn't succeed across the board, it winds up getting awfully close...No Time to Die brings this chapter to a satisfying conclusion.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: While No Time To Die may not be a perfect film, it's a great vehicle for Daniel Craig to bid goodbye to the greatest role of his career, and simultaneously pay tribute to the greatest Bond film in the process.
reviews.author: Maxance Vincent

reviews.text: It's hard to forgive No Time to Die for its sins because of the nature of its unevenness.
reviews.author: Ciara Wardlow

reviews.text: Malek is criminally underused, and the character is so absurd that he feels like a parody of what a Bond villain should be.
reviews.author: Kaila Hale-Stern

reviews.text: Fukunaga deserves credit for taking the character and adding real stakes to his 15-year story arc.
reviews.author: Mark Daniell

reviews.text: This 25th film in the franchise is at once on brand with the two dozen films that preceded it, while managing new possibilities for the almost 60-year-old series.
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: The caretakers of the Intellectual Property known as James Bond, knowing that their newest effort would be the last one to star Daniel Craig, decided to spare no expense to make this an "epic" entry in the series. I just wish there were less of it
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: [No Time to Die is] more than a victory lap... nonetheless, there are also many scenes that are no more than padding. This especially applies to the action scenes. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Even with a lackluster villain, No Time To Die is a satisfying, thoughtful, and at times genuinely compelling conclusion to Daniel Craig's run as Bond that's just as full of emotional beats as it is action set pieces.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Craig clearly demonstrates his dramatic chops in this emotional, highly enjoyable conclusion.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: While No Time to Die lags in parts, it feels like the fitting finale Daniel Craig has been waiting for.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: They toughened Craig-as-Bond up only to soften him, uncharacteristically, in this film. To love the film you have to love JB as a person, which is odd for a spy & his legacy.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: We are given the opportunity to get to know their version of James Bond one final time. Is this the very best Bond? I wouldn't know, but I do know this is the very best send-off a Bond could get.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: "No Time To Die" does for the James Bond franchise what "The Last Jedi" sought to do for "Star Wars."
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: Fukunaga delivers a rousing finale to close out an era while Daniel Craig gives us a final definitive performance as the most vulnerable and down-to-earth representation of Ian Fleming's character.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: As the closing of a chapter No Time To Die works exceptionally well, a heady yet comforting mix of nostalgia and the shock of the unexpected.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: An underdeveloped villain and wieldy run time can't keep the visual flair and consistent fun from giving Craig a meaningful and compelling send off.
reviews.author: Aaron Dicer

reviews.text: No Time to Die is cinematic in every sense of the word. With a brilliant final performance from Daniel Craig, incredible action sequences and an emotional core, No Time to Die is a worthy conclusion to the franchise.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: It's worth the wait and is absolutely worth going to see on the big screen. It's big, bold, fun, and even more lighthearted in some ways than it has been in years but then hits you with an emotional depth you won't see coming.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: Had they nailed the villain here - this would have undoubtedly been one of the best entries in the entire Bond franchise.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Craig leaves knowing that this 25th film featuring Ian Fleming's heroic 007 has him giving a grand-finale worthy performance.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: It has everything you expect from Bond and appropriately honors Daniel Craig for his service to the Queen.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: There might be many inevitable changes and shifts for the James Bond movies in the future, but Daniel Craig got to go out with a bang.
reviews.author: Alif Majeed

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's turn in the iconic role comes to a glorious end with No Time to Die, a definite highlight not just in his era but in the franchise overall.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: It was overlong and it got heavy in a way that I'm not sure a Bond film needs to. I admire what it was trying to do, but there was just a weightiness to it.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: No Time To Die is an absolute triumph, not just as a thrilling conclusion to Daniel Craig's era of Bond, but as one of the best in the series.
reviews.author: Jake Tropila

reviews.text: Daniel Craig brought depth to the James Bond character and in his last outing as 007, Craig brings heart to 007 in a satisfying and bittersweet way.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: In many ways, No Time to Die is a perfect microcosm of the Craig films: parts of it are undeniably great, but it's also wildly uneven and frustratingly tepid in places
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: Craig is as cool as ever as Bond, and he commences with his derring-do, dispatching baddies with considerable aplomb... [O]verall this Bond delivers what fans have come to expect from a 007 film, no more, no less.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: If Rami Malek as supervillain Lyutsifer Safin is more method acting than genuine menace, well, so be it. There is much here to cherish as loose ends are neatly tied, legacies are assured, and the pyrotechnics deliver.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: [T]here is a finality and harmony in Bond's story that we haven't really had before and that is what makes this version of Bond a game-changer.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's best performance to date as James Bond.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: No Time to Die proves that the decades-old James Bond franchise has reached a dead end. The turn toward sadism that began with Daniel Craig's angry, sinister interpretation of 007 has reached an unconscionable level of heartlessness.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: No Time to Die will probably be looked back upon as the best of the best era of Bond films...an amazing Bond entry, a terrific culmination of the Craig era and a perfectly fitting farewell
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: The only reason this isn't the most embarrassing thing Rami Malek has ever done is because he won an Oscar for a Bryan Singer movie.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: While not a complete home run, No Time to Die was worth the wait. See this one in a movie theater if you can. Craig has earned that much, and the film more than justifies a big-screen experience.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: "No Time to Die" ends the Daniel Craig era with explosions and nanobots instead of wit and genuine emotional pathos.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: A little of that goes a long way, and the problem with No Time to Die is that it's trying for big, bruising feelings at all times. Over two hours and 40 minutes, the pathos wears you out.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: There were ups and downs in the actor's 15-year tenure as 007, but his greatest accomplishment was making an iconic character seem human.
reviews.author: Miles Surrey

reviews.text: NO TIME TO DIE is a viscerally effective send-off for Daniel Craig's tenure. Still, a deep thematic confusion prevents it from resonating beyond the increasingly narrow confines of what a James Bond movie is seemingly allowed to be.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: I'm not one for nostalgia, especially when it comes to Bond movies. But really (sigh), they don't write 'em like that anymore.
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's final moments as Bond rank among the most moving sequences in the history of this franchise, which has long favored the fantastic and the eye-popping in favor of genuine emotional stakes.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: I was surprised and pleased by how well this entry... honors the compact the series has made with audiences over the decades while retooling it for today.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: No Time to Die retires Old Man Bond in reverent yet melancholy fashion,
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: No Time to Die tends to lag a bit around the three-quarter mark and it sometimes feels driven by fumes of determination, but when it's done, No Time to Die has brought Craig's tenure to a strong and worthy conclusion.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Is Craig's poignant farewell the best of the actor's run? I'd put the emotionality of Skyfall and the eye-popping Casino Royale ahead, but No Time to Die unquestionably makes returning to theaters a reason to live.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: This is a fittingly emotional end for the actor who played the most vulnerable Bond.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: At 163 minutes, this maximalist farewell is the Long Goodbye of Bond movies. Fun it's not. But it thrills and excites just as much as it puffs up its emotionally anemic superspy with all the feels.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: Writers Fukunaga, Neal Purvis, Robert Wade and Phoebe Waller-Bridge keep that breathtaking pace going for most of the movie, giving fans plenty of opportunities to see Craig's Bond and his cohorts in action one last time.
reviews.author: Brandy McDonnell

reviews.text: I was left neither shaken nor stirred but rather perplexed.
reviews.author: Rosalynn Try-Hane

reviews.text: Fukunaga and editors Elliot Graham and Tom Cross are champs at keeping the scenes jumping, blending them into each other in a dazzling array.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: All in all, No Time To Die delivered a satisfying resolution to the Craig Bond films.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: Beautiful people abound, and 007 still knows how to fill out a tux. I had a reasonably good time at it. But, as I watched this latest installment the thought also occurred to me: Has James Bond become irrelevant?
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Alas, even the exotic locales, exciting visuals, and a most welcome, high-level cast (including Naomie Harris, Ben Whishaw, Jeffrey Wright, and Ana de Armas), can't save the film from its overhanging, glaring weakness: superfluousness.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: "No Time to Die" is a fitting finale for one of the best Bonds ever and while James Bond will most certainly return, Craig has forever changed what it means to be 007.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: It's a testament to Fukunaga's direction that, even as mysteries pile up faster than bodies, we're never completely at sea. And there are plenty of wild distractions to entertain us while we're on our way to solving this riddle.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: The once-insouciant spy hero became intense and obsessive when Daniel Craig started to play him, only to become mawkish and sentimental in his final chapter.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: It's as crisply entertaining as any of the previous Craig movies, but circuitous in its quest to tie them all together.
reviews.author: John Wenzel

reviews.text: Maybe by the time the next Bond film comes out in four to seven years, no one will remember or care what happened in this one. But it sure left me feeling like a bridge had been unnecessarily burnt.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Nomi's presence in the film-along with the fact that, finally, Ben Whishaw as Q has been allowed to play the character as gay-suggests a new and bright future for the franchise.
reviews.author: Jo Livingstone

reviews.text: It feels, like 2019's Avengers: Endgame, like the end of a cycle, a grand epic about sacrifice and the future of mankind. But it also gives us a Bond with more emotion and maybe even humanity than many of his predecessors seemed to possess.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: No Time To Die marks an exciting and entertaining sendoff to Craig's legendary tenure as James Bond, but the real scene stealers of the film are the women, especially Lashana Lynch.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: A moving swansong performance. Farewell great, craggy Craig. Ana de Armas is great fun.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: What it lacks in speed in makes up for in attitude, as the glum mood of the previous couple of Craig titles is leavened with humor and a certain pleasing deftness.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: This is Craig's finest moment as an actor, a magnificent performance of power and range that makes his Bond by far the most human and involving of the six actors to carry the name.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Not perfect but entertaining and a fine farewell to Craig in the part.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Where No Time to Die stands out the most is in its treatment of women. These are no Bond girls but women with agency. Ana de Armas plays Paloma, a CIA agent who helps Bond. But even if there's chemistry between them, Paloma is immune to Bond's charms.
reviews.author: Patricia Puentes

reviews.text: A solid ending to the Daniel Craig era. A tad long, but watching Craig's last mission is nostalgic and satisfactory. Definitely was worth the wait. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: ...the perfect Bond film, full of spectacular action, romance, and intrigue - everything one could hope for.
reviews.author: Kevin Brackett

reviews.text: This quintet of pictures has packed a more poignant punch than any of the previous Bond movies.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The film ends with enough fireworks to effectively cap this miniseries of Bond adventures.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Despite a sappy ending that surprises in all the wrong ways, Daniel Craig's fifth and final go-round as 007 cements his reputation as the gold-standard James Bond of the 21st century and lays down a challenge for anyone who dares to follow him.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: It rushes like adrenaline through the bloodstream and make Craig's final mission as James Bond as exciting as it is tragic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: This was an emotional end to an epic arc by Daniel Craig as 007. Cary Joji Fukunaga did a great job with the action and getting really solid performances out of everyone. The film took risks and despite the nearly 3 hour runtime, they mostly paid off.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Given the difficulty at play, what No Time to Die encompasses is a welcomed return to form, re-establishing the essence of the tried and tested formula, but also dares to push Bond into new territory.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Arguably the greatest James Bond filming ever, 'No Time To Die' easily qualifies as an exercise in exclamatory adjectives.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: It's often exciting, but there's something inward and agonized about the thrills, and the insouciance of Connery's epoch, for better or worse, seems like ancient history.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: it works as a fitting sendoff to Craig and his Bond films, which took big risks with an iconic character that, for the most part, paid off. "James Bond Will Return," as the closing credits promise. But he'll never be the same.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: It's Craig's swan song, but Bond will return.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: The preamble to a face-to-face between Blofeld and Bond echoes with the library of paintings built by Francis Bacon of men in cages, caught in booths, Popes struck to scream by encroaching captivity, mortality, madness.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Rami Malek's character is another example of how the franchise has a real villain problem. One thing is for sure, the explosive ending is certainly well earned and long overdue.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: No Time To Die serves as a solid finale for Daniel Craig's tenure as James Bond, with his performance and the action sequences making up for a sprawling runtime and unwieldy screenplay.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: "No Time to Die" is a good time at the movies.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Fukunaga gives Craig a stunning send-off as Bond, in this beautifully shot and epic adventure.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Director Cary Joji Fukunaga breaks visual ground in the enchanting blues and purples of nocturnal Cuba and Jamaica set pieces, and bursts of eerie emotional tension stamp his trademark on action set pieces.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: A more mature Bond with a richer performance than ever by Daniel Craig.
reviews.author: Michael Medved

reviews.text: Craig gets to say a fitting farewell to a character he elevated for modern audiences.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Overall, No Time To Die is well worth the wait and a worthy end to the reign of Craig's excellent Bond.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: [No Time to Die attempts] to "modernize" the James Bond character by stripping him of traits deemed problematic while also clinging steadfastly (and often embarrassingly) to the series' most meaningless of traditions.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: In other words, nothing new. Same slick package, different psychopathic enemy. Yes, it's time to go back to the cinema!
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: Gives us something we may have never had in a Bond movie - closure.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: More epic drama than raucous spy adventure, this beefy thriller is a terrific cap on Daniel Craig's five-film series as 007
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Spends so much time on its sentimental farewell to Bond that it seems to forget what made him worth watching in the first place.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: For a lumbering, 163-minute blockbuster it's surprisingly light on its feet, if still egregiously overlong.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: An enjoyable ride on the way to closure for this iteration of the character.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: [It] gives us a number of reasons to appreciate the Bond he [Craig] has been -- as well as to wonder what kind of Bond he could have been.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's last hurrah as 007 ticks every hoped-for Bond-shaped box in a smart, absorbing thriller with some surprising twists.
reviews.author: Terry Staunton

reviews.text: It's a poignant pleasure to see Daniel Craig as Bond on the big screen one last time, even if the movie around him is seldom as good as he is.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: There's a sense of dread and melancholy that hangs over the film and it's all the better for it.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: It's a hard-working attempt to reconcile the Bond rituals with a series-finale emotional weight that these movies have been accumulating (with mixed success) since 2006.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Daniel Craig leaves the franchise having made the biggest impact on the character since Sean Connery set the rules more than half a century ago.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: In the era of COVID and Brexit, much of this overstuffed adventure feels redundant, farcical, inconsequential, and desperate. But Ana de Armas and Lashana Lynch show us the way to a future for 007.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Craig's dedication to the role has left us both shaken AND stirred, which I guess, is only fitting.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: No Time to Die aims to marry the Bond of the present with the Bond of the past, injecting the grittier recent films with some old-school franchise silliness seen through the current lens.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: It concludes in a bittersweet way, making it clear that yes, this is the end ... but that as always, James Bond will return. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Daniel Craig goes out with a bang...
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: It entertains and it's definitely worth a trip to the theater...sampling itself while straddling old and new...
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

reviews.text: It's ambitious, sprawling, and sometimes shockingly counter to tradition for the series. But it's also hugely effective.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: While there are some great moments, it's near impossible to sustain chase scenes and fist fights and love making and villain 'splaining for such an extended amount of time.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: The action sequences -- especially that opener in Italy -- are crisp and well choreographed, with exceptional aerial photography and camera work in tight confines as the mayhem goes down. Like much in the film, though, they tend to go on too long.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Despite the usual quota of big action set-pieces, 'No Time to Die' is a glum, undernourished affair, lacking the frisson of the best Bond pictures.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: ...has a self-awareness that's suffocating.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's fifth and final mission as Ian Fleming's super suave/sexy 007 is one of the actor's best in the series - but it's not as good as "Casino Royale" or "Skyfall."
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Produced beautifully, it's one of the year's best tent-poles. But what you'll remember most is how much heart Craig puts into it. And yours might just ache considerably after the film ends.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: No Time to Die caps off films which have elevated the James Bond franchise into something they rarely were before: fine examples of artistic, dramatic craft.
reviews.author: Tony Black

reviews.text: Managing Editor and Chief Film Critic Jason Gorber weighs in on this newest instalment and gives us his take on this "worthy yet slightly redundant" addition to the 007 canon. Watch his review below now:
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: What was initially touted as the long-overdue reboot of the stodgy old 007 franchise into a lean, mean, take-me-seriously-now machine itself now feels unmistakably like a creaky, lumbering nostalgia throwback to the 'Good Old Days' of the pre-2010s
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: More serious and long, but a fitting emotional send off for this chapter of the franchise. Apprehensive of the 2 hour 45 minute running time, weren't sure would be too much of a good thing, but Craig's performances surpasses what he's given to work with.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: No Time to Die is not only a fitting last chapter to the Craig era, but a Bond movie that dares to tread wholly new ground for the 59-year-old franchise.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: Some things are worth the wait.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: It's hardly the best Bond film, but what screenwriters Purvis, Wade, Fukunaga, and Waller-Bridge have given us here is an emotionally-satisfying, exciting, and solidly-entertaining entry in the franchise that delivers exactly where it needs to.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: Daniel Craig makes his royal exit in "No Time to Die," a handsome if entirely too long James Bond adventure that struggles with James Bond's place in the modern world.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The film's occasional overreaches aren't always a negative; the high points are very high and, when it's all over, most viewers will remember them.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: No Time To Die is a fitting farewell to Daniel Craig as James Bond, and the drama is one of the best in the franchise.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: Craig goes out in style in one of the finest films of the series, an archetypal Bond movie at its core that feels fresh and showcases impeccable filmmaking in every department.
reviews.author: James Kleinmann

reviews.text: No matter where the series goes from here, they've given Daniel Craig a great send-off in No Time to Die, even if it's not as spectacular as some of his earlier entries.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: The franchise pulls out the stops in giving Bond a soul and prepping the field for the next generation of spy stars.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: As it turns out, it cannot quite pull everything off but, much like its venerable hero, it does not go down without a fight.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: A darn good respectable finale for the Daniel Craig era of Bond.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Respect should be paid to Fukunaga and his team for taking a risk, doing something that most corporate franchises would scuttle away from.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: More like a greatest hits checklist than a fully formed film.
reviews.author: Joey Morona

reviews.text: Craig's fifth and final outing as the secret MI6 superagent James Bond is also a fittingly complicated and ultimately perversely satisfying send-off for the actor...
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: I appreciate director Fukunaga's confident, swank handling of the action, and his juggling of tones.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Simply put, love has been given more value than pleasure, and the investment has succeeded.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Fukunaga brings smooth, effortlessly handsome style to a harmonious, pointedly nostalgic adventure acknowledging the cultural changes that rendered parts of the Bond mythology "problematic" while delivering something true to what audiences expect.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: "No Time to Die" falls somewhere in an unremarkable middle between Craig's best Bond films ("Casino Royale," "Skyfall") and the lesser efforts ("Spectre," "Quantum of Solace").
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: This is one of the most emotional Bond movies where things comes full circle for Daniel Craig. While his tenure does not end in an all-time-high fashion, I can say that No Time To Die is a bold and memorable finale for a game-changing Bond era.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Where previous Bond movies either leaned heavily into darker or more campy tones, Craig's final film as Bond merges both elements to create a character that feels entirely its own.
reviews.author: Joshua Mackey

reviews.text: Amid seriously high stakes, Craig makes you root for Bond like never before in a swan song that'll leave die-hards shaken, if not stirred.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: As a movie, Bond-related or otherwise, it's just fine: sometimes intriguing, sometimes not, sometimes boring, sometimes not. It's a bit more successful if we think of it instead as a tribute to the Craig era, and to the star himself.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Confronted with his own sense of finality, Craig rises to meet the moment, delivering a Bond for the ages that none of us will soon forget, even when the next guy takes on the 007 moniker.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: Fukunaga seems indebted to the sixth Bond outing On Her Majesty's Secret Service in a way that has fascinating implications for the series and its future.
reviews.author: Conor O'Donnell

reviews.text: Some might find that No Time to Die, clocking in at just under three hours, is a long journey. But there are enough action sequences- some of the best since the crane fight in the opening scene of Casino Royale-to make time move quickly.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: The coordinates of the film's formal device do not fit, just as the narrative sieve. In fact, one is almost tempted to thank Fukunaga for allowing things to happen almost automatically, flat. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aarón Rodríguez Serrano

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's historically uneven 007 gets a solid send-off.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: For anyone who's grown up with Bond, as I have, or found themselves re-energised by Craig's muscular turn in the role, this is a big moment, a big film and one you'll definitely want to see on the big screen.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The frustration, as he bows out, is that in No Time to Die Craig has rediscovered that groove of Casino Royale.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: It's bloated and flabby around the mid-section and prone to moments of confusion. But it's also the first Bond movie in forever that attempts real change...
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: A great closing for the cycle of films starring Daniel Craig and one of the best James Bond films in the history of the franchise.
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: With an impressive high-stakes mission and an emotional drive, No Time To Die is a truly fitting & heartfelt swan song for Daniel Craig
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: No Time to Die is the perfect James Bond movie; action-packed, satisfying, and surprisingly heartfelt, Cary Joji Fukunaga proves an ideal fit for this franchise and helps make sure Daniel Craig, who is phenomenal here, ends his tenure as 007 in style.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: Bond is back, cinema is back, and it feels just great.
reviews.author: Denis Mann

reviews.text: It will probably leave its fan base satisfied to be once again shaken ... and stirred.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's cruel, blunt take on 007 remains incompatible with the franchise's need to give audiences the comfortable ride they demand.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: The 25th James Bond film-and last featuring star Daniel Craig as the superspy-is surprisingly long and unexciting, save for an electrifying turn from Ana de Armas.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Mounted on the grand scale we have come to expect from Bond films, No Time To Die is a fitting finale for Daniel Craig's version of the spy who cannot be allowed to depart.
reviews.author: Scroll Staff

reviews.text: Instead of a celebration Craig leaves Bond in an overlong stylized whimper.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: No Time To Die is best summed up as the perfect Bond experience. Don't miss this one in the big screens.
reviews.author: Sunayana Suresh

reviews.text: Daniel Craig loses no opportunity to demonstrate why he has had such a salutary impact on the evolution of James Bond. His Bond is more impulsive, sensitive and passionate than ever before.
reviews.author: Saibal Chatterjee

reviews.text: An exciting if uneven final turn for Daniel Craig as James Bond
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: This film is sexist, beautifully shot, well-paced and filled with Bondian brutality and Bondian babes, as Daniel Craig's wounded creature of a secret agent has his last adventure.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: No Time to Die is a talky, sometimes-dour, imperfect farewell to Daniel Craig's Bond. However, it's also just fun enough to remind audiences what draws us to this series in the first place.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Above all, it manages to connect properly with its predecessors to offer a dignified and emphatic outcome, like never before in the franchise. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Del Río

reviews.text: As for Craig, he leaves the stage with nothing left to prove. He is, for me, the best Bond of them all.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Those who make their way to the multiplex for No Time to Die will at least be treated to plenty of eye-popping spectacle.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Daniel Craig says bye-bye to Bond with the haunting but talky revenge tale No Time to Die.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: Some action scenes are truly worthy of note, like watching Ana de Armas kick some tail. But the wows are all followed with too much disengagement.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: The Woke Army has won. The masculine icon of a 60 year reign is over. An archetype who was desired by all who met him , male and female, is now monogamous and madly in love. He almost cries.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: It's clear that this is Craig's fifth and final film in the franchise not only because he has made it known in the media but because the film truly has a "let's go out with a bang" mentality all the way through.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: Despite some runtime and minor story issues, No Time to Die is a fabulous send-off for Daniel Craig and the best action movie of the year.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Cary Joji Fukunaga has shot a gorgeous movie and filled it with plenty of arresting, dynamic images...but he's completely failed to pace it properly after [a] delightful first half.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: There is a lot to like in No Time to Die. It's great to see strong women in major positions, though Lynch's Nomi ultimately takes a backseat in the grand finale.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: James Bond will return. He just might not be the same.
reviews.author: Matthew Razak

reviews.text: Ana de Armas' sparkling presence highlights the surprising droopiness of much of the rest of the movie.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: The story dares to go places one couldn't imagine even the early Craig movies would go, and caps off this era for the franchise in a bittersweet but fittingly poignant manner.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: No Time to Die truly is going to go down as one of the best pictures this year.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: (The movie's) biggest mistake is that, instead of taking the franchise forward - eventually, a new actor will be given a license to kill - it spends a lot of time looking over the series' cinematic shoulder.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Director Cary Joji Fukunaga does fine job mustering his huge cast, impressive CGI and good, old-fashioned action to bring us an entertaining and flashy entry to the Bond story.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: The set pieces are spectacular. They are an amalgamation of what makes Bond films exciting - the over-the-top campy action, carefully followed by the more realistic and exhilarating stuff.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: A kind of pastiche of the series proper - with Craig's mirthless, fragile Bond, out of place as well as time.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: There is a pleasing finality to it for everyone ... but there's also a palpable sense that it's a step too far, and the series may never try such big swings again.
reviews.author: Joshua Starnes

reviews.text: No Time To Die has all the ingredients of a great Bond film and some heart too.
reviews.author: Jamal Grootboom

reviews.text: It's extremely rare for a film of this scale to be this affecting.
reviews.author: Thomas Barrie

reviews.text: Soodbye, Daniel Craig. If you weren't the best Bond (and trust me, I think you probably were), you were definitely the only man who could have made him this interestingly human without sacrificing all of the cool. Nobody did it better.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Most characters and actors should hope for such a grand farewell, and a grand farewell it was.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: No Time To Die not only marks the 25th instalment in the James Bond franchise, but it also ends Daniel Craig's 15 year tenure as Bond and ensures that Craig's 007 goes out on an all-time high.
reviews.author: Niall Browne

reviews.text: Cary Fukunaga seized upon what could have been a soured, if not poisoned, chalice -- after the bloated disappointment of 2015's Spectre -- with both hands and made it his own, giving Daniel Craig the fitting tribute to his 15-year commitment to the role.
reviews.author: Matthew Anderson

reviews.text: The new installment is exciting for its energy and scale, despite its flaws and derivative themes, and makes a lovely valediction for its star.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The spiritual sequel of my favorite Bond film, "On Her Majesty's Secret Service" (1969). Craig's goodbye knows the value of emotion over action. Incredible movie.
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: Add up the performances, the passion of the filmmaking, the scale of the story, and the links back to the previous films and No Time to Die has a lot to cover, but does it well
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: Director Cary Joji Fukunaga... brings rhythm, dynamism and humor to Craig's farewell. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: By the end, the movie itself feels worn out, uncertain what it is we're all doing here.
reviews.author: Sam Adams

reviews.text: No Time to Die is fun, action-packed, and a less womanizing James Bond. One of the more kid-friendly Bond movies.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: Aims high and falls just short
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: "No Time to Die" has moments of pleasure, lots of them, but ultimately it feels heavy in a way a Bond movie shouldn't; its pacing is off and it can't quite sell the earnestness and even sentimentality of much of its storyline.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Craig reveals himself as perhaps the most generous actor to have inhabited the role. And not only toward the rest of the cast, but toward the very idea of Bond itself.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: Whatever the niggles, it exists on such a heightened plane of gloriously-rendered insanity it's hard not to get swept up in it.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: "An incredibly bold, brave, fitting ending...not a slam dunk, but it's incredibly ballsy and there's a lot to enjoy & admire."
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: No Time To Die might feature some of the best action to come out of the Daniel Craig era, but his swan song as the character of James Bond is dragged down by a muddled story and an incredibly boring Bond girl.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's final James Bond film is a tragic melodrama masquerading as a muscular action picture.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: An exhilarating and thoughtful send-off for Daniel Craig. Now how about an Ana de Armas spin-off?
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: [It's] not the best James Bond movie to star Daniel Craig, but it's got enough thrilling action to make up for some hokey dialogue and questionable creative decisions. It's a guaranteed crowd-pleaser for people who are inclined to like James Bond films.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: No Time To Die is the proper finale for Craig's Bond. This film is bold, visually stunning, and full of classic throwback moments. There is a lot to this story, but it all builds to a climactic and satisfying conclusion.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: This may not be the Bond we want, but could it be the Bond we need?
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Best Daniel Craig Bond movie since Casino Royale, yet an ending sure to divide fans. Still, Fukunaga modernizes Bond while staying faithful to the formula. Very entertaining.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: dramatically impressive, wryly funny, and profoundly emotional. Craig gives it all he's got left in the tank
reviews.author: Chris Hunneysett

reviews.text: That it manages deep soul-searching, tangible affection, and a real punch to the gut, all while also delivering some thrilling action set-pieces, is no small thing.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: The problem is that, both thematically and structurally, it's damn near the same as Skyfall. So those risks are visible from miles away.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Craig is having more fun than ever, here, as if Logan Lucky and Knives Out propelled him to dig deeper.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: What fascinated me and satisfied me the most about this James Bond film is how smooth it goes down. It's not forgetting the gadgets, the beautiful women, the swagger, the cool intro sequence, or a lounge tune to set the mood.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: At this particular historical moment, I'd say we could use a funnier, less broody Bond. Pain, we've all had our fill of. I have no idea in what direction this series is headed, but I sure hope the fun returns.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: More concerned with sending off its star in lackluster fashion than telling a compelling or intriguing story.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: For a series that so often is defined by the willy antics of its antagonists, No Time to Die makes the gruesome mistake of saving the worst for last.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Mission accomplished.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: What follows those bursts of typically Bondian elan is ponderously weighted and thinly plotted... Leave this somber serialization to other franchises and let 007 get back to business-which should, ideally, be a pleasure.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: An emotional, gripping end to this version of Bond
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: "No Time To Die" may not be perfect, or as good as Daniel Craig's other James Bond films. It nonetheless serves its purpose as a sly social cinematic barometer. Right or wrong, things change.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Every single action sequence carries emotional weight, while the pacing, energetic cutting and camera movement help to make a near three-hour film pass in a flash.
reviews.author: Demetrios Matheou

reviews.text: No Time to Die shows signs of emerging from an over-deliberated, market-sensitised production process. Much too protracted at 163 minutes, it delivers the set-pieces without ever trying to connect them with any urgency, almost like an anthology or re-mix.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: A rousing score from Hans Zimmer, excellent editing, and a jaunty narrative mark this as a highpoint for contemporary Bond offerings and a sterling cinematic return for Fukunaga.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: A huge undertaking, and while "Die" is visually impressive, it's chained to the haphazard storytelling that's been reworked over the last 15 years, finding the effort most concerned about relationships that never meant much to begin with.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: It takes James Bond, humanizes him, exposes vulnerability, and dares to trek uncharted storytelling grounds. No Time to Die triumphantly reaches devastatingly stirring heights
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Who knew that the sight of James Bond picking up a stuffed rabbit named Dou-dou would evoke not only a chuckle, but a lump in our throats?
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: While Skyfall would have been a better send-off for him, No Time to Die is nonetheless a showcase for a complex and first-in-class performance from the best James Bond we've ever had.
reviews.author: Matt Purslow

reviews.text: A disappointing swan song for Daniel Craig's era as the character leans too much on fondness for past adventures without leaving its own mark.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Now, in his final installment, Daniel Craig solidifies that out of all the Bonds, he was the most emotional and, in turn, philosophical.
reviews.author: Diandra Reviews

reviews.text: While not a perfect stamp on Daniel Craig's last 007 film, 'No Time To Die' shows why his time was so vital to the character's growth.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: It's bold and ambitious, yet it exudes confidence and moves with such drive, you do not feel most of its admittedly long 163-minute running time.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: You can feel the film dragging its heels toward its destination, nobody wanting to say their goodbyes to the franchise, and I'm generous enough and willing to grant them some leeway on that front because Daniel Craig's James Bond has earned it.
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Craig is having a blast with a script that adds nuances, some blatantly comical... the rest of the performers (especially the female ones) are freed from those mere auxiliary roles. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yago García

reviews.text: If "No Time to Die" were 90 minutes long, it might be worth yours.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Craig leaves the series in a mammoth, 163-minute extravaganza that audiences will be enjoying for decades. It's a lovely thing to see.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: While Bond's never been the most complex of onscreen characters, past attempts at fleshing him out in On Her Majesty's Secret Service and Craig's debut, Casino Royale, have been surpassed here.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: An epic, breathtaking conclusion to the Craig era of Bond. After close to two years in the waiting for its release, audiences will finally be able to see it and experience the closure that Craig has found with the fitting end to his run as 007.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: Keep in mind the deconstructions only work because 20 previous movies proved reliable standalone entries. At least the defining trait of Craig's era will be that none of his movies are interchangeable.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: There's nothing here that's hasn't been done better in one of the other Craig movies.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Daniel Craig takes James Bond into uncharted territory with a powerfully emotional and epic performance. No Time to Die is hands down the best finale for an actor portraying 007. There are a lot of surprises here.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: By whatever metrics you measure a Bond movie -- tight plotting, gnarly villains, emotional sincerity -- Craig's final outing is a rip-roaring success.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: This Bond's overall arc from modishly merciless killing machine to aging assassin with the familial feels comes off as a treacly sop to psychological complexity.
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: "No Time to Die" comes full circle and toasts Daniel Craig in a tasteful manner that earns its payoff.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The kind of finale that suggests Craig should have hung up his tuxedo and finished his last vodka martini immediately after Skyfall.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: No Time to Die has its share of problems but was definitely worth the wait.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: Nobody does it better, but this woke-free Bond runs out of gas when it's needed most of all
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: Doesn't try to reinvent the Bond wheel, but it also doesn't do enough to inject some fresh air into a franchise that's become a bit of a dated flat tire.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: No Time to Die makes sure that my eyes are following each and every oh-whoa stunt. As well as guaranteeing that I actually care about whether (or, really, how) Bond gets out of this one.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Bond movies have to try to be a lot of different things for a lot of different people, but "No Time to Die" had one job: send Daniel Craig off right. It sticks that particular landing.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Fukunaga directs with a real slickness and style, and fans will rejoice in a globe-trotting plot that takes in Cuba and Norway.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: "Delivers the expected rush of thrills, cars, explosions, gadgets and so on, while also pushing emotional buttons you don't normally associate with the Bond franchise."
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: With a bold direction and epic visuals, No Time to Die not only reminds audiences of how good Bond films can be but also paves a new and modern path for 007.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Craig might be done with Bond, but No Time to Die reminds audiences why they fell for him in the first place.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: Along with a weak script and underwhelming directing from Cary Fukunaga, it simply sacrifices too much of the viscerally, thrillingly unapologetic anti-hero that has towered across six decades of cinema.
reviews.author: Stefan Kyriazis

reviews.text: This is a serious film, and it will leave you seriously blown away.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: No Time To Die is forgettable in all the places that usually count -- it's a Bond movie with little excitement or panache.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: With his fifth movie as 007, Craig is so extraordinary he leaves only scorched earth behind. There will be other Bonds for those who want them. For everyone else, there's Craig.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: The send-off Craig's Bond (probably) deserves.
reviews.author: Adam Woodward

reviews.text: "No Time to Die" is a terrific movie: an up-to-the-minute, down-to-the-wire James Bond thriller with a satisfying neo-classical edge.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Even if the two-and-three-quarter hour running time is occasionally a slog, it ultimately delivers.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: As Bond swan songs go, it's a fond farewell: faithfully bridging the old world and the new until the last, deathless postscript.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: It's still the same tired nonsense, just longer, and all the added elements to give the story and the characters emotional heft mostly fail as a result.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Fukunaga reverses out of the dead end of Spectre, then does wheelies. His trick is to take everything the other Craig movies muted and crank them to 11.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: It still feels a little shocking that Daniel Craig's time in the tux is through, but for his final performance, he does deliver some of his best work.
reviews.author: Jason Guerrasio

reviews.text: No Time To Die is a fitting swan song for Daniel Craig's James Bond era: moody, action-packed, imperfect and surprisingly bold.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: A good 30 minutes could have made it to the cutting room floor. Still, there are few fans of the franchise who will leave No Time to Die dissatisfied. It's the third-best Daniel Craig Bond outing.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: ...quite likely the most satisfying Bond film ever made, and it is absolutely the right film - Bond or otherwise - for this moment in time.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: No Time to Die ends Daniel Craig's time as James Bond in epic style. It's everything you want out of 007, including a bit of emotion. It's long, but it earns your time.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Despites its ample flaws, I mostly had fun with No Time to Die and found it to be a fitting conclusion to Craig's memorable yet uneven tenure as Bond.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: No Time to Die stumbles from too many principal characters and a disconnect in tones outlandish and highly serious (the more outlandish stuff works better). The bold ending frankly feels more telegraphed than naturally affecting.
reviews.author: Samuel R. Murrian

reviews.text: For those who've taken Daniel Craig's Bond as their concerns: Their wait is worth it. His final scene is the most heartbreaking sequence in the franchise's history.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: No Time To Die is a misguided, meandering slog. [Daniel Craig] deserved a far better franchise send-off than this.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: Every time it feels like it is about to start to drag, the adrenaline and action start back up again! Visually stunning and action packed, a great send off to Craig!
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: You will be on the edge of your seats the entire time. It ends with what may be the cliffhanger of all cliffhangers, or a finale for the ages.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: No Time to Die may have taken forever to get here, but the wait was more than worth it. Whoever steps in next has enormous shoes to fill.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson should be applauded for taking so many bold risks. The gosmacking ending, in fact, may be the biggest in Bond history.
reviews.author: Alex Flood

reviews.text: The picture isn't merely overstuffed, it's detrimentally overstuffed.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Craig's is a Bond who's secure enough in his manhood to let de Armas' Paloma or Lynch's Nomi shine - and strong enough to bring some emotional weight, and even tears, to 007's world-saving mission.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: What Cary Joji Fukunaga has managed to do here is capture the essence of Bond without contrivance, all the while bringing the character and world firmly into the present day.
reviews.author: Stefan Pape

reviews.text: A satisfactory valediction to the longest reign so far in the Bond dynasty
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: It's a fitting swansong for Craig's bruising Bond, although the increased sensitivity and emotion required this time around is an awkward fit
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Polished and filled with life, the Daniel Craig-era of Bond has never felt better. What a way to close this chapter!
reviews.author: EJ Moreno
