reviews.text: The great Phoebe Waller-Bridge contributed to the screenplay; it's nice to think that the "Fleabag" creator might have come up with the funniest stuff.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: An epic swan song for Daniel Craig as 007. Reintroduces some humor and fun into the series after too long of an absence.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's fifth and final outing as Bond is replete with fantastic action sequences and an emotional center despite the final act being shaky.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Nobody did it better.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: Even a disappointing villain can't detract from a bold, satisfying climax to Daniel Craig's time in the tux.
reviews.author: Matt Maytum

reviews.text: Fukunaga's direction is crisp and assured, if occasionally languid, and the script creaks under the weight of its myriad responsibilities to both its star and franchise. But it hits where it counts.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: 'No Time To Die' is pretty good when it's focused on just being "the next James Bond movie," but it stumbles in the back half as a direct sequel to 'Spectre.'
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: The longest Bond movie of all. It feels long, too. But it packs in so much that you can hardly complain.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Assiduously builds on everything that the recent Bond movies have established, in a way earlier incarnations generally didn't.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: It's all pretty fun and pretty ridiculous. The problem is the movie doesn't always realize this should be a hoot.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Taking over from Sam Mendes, 44-year-old Cary Joji Fukunaga is 007s first American director. He's clearly having fun.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: There's plenty to gawk at, and to argue over, in this episode - yet No Time To Die is oddly lacking in pleasure or real wit.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: No Time to Die feels like an organic evolution, a way to leave the winking sexism of old in the rear-view mirror once and for all.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: This is Bond film that dutifully ticks all the boxes - but brilliantly, often doesn't feel like a Bond film at all. For a 007 who strived to bring humanity to larger-than-life hero, it's a fitting end to the Craig era.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: In his final turn as 007, Craig exits the franchise with a bang - as well as many crashes and several wallops.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: It's a good film that's been forced to rattle around in the Bond universe like a loose cog.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: It's better than good. It's magnificent.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Daniel Craig's best incarnation of an iconic role, an iteration that sees Bond travel to emotional spaces the character has never been to before, at least not since On Her Majesty's Secret Service or in certain passages of Ian Fleming's books.
reviews.author: Jason Solomons

reviews.text: We've been expecting you, Mr Bond, for quite some time - and what a joy and relief it is to have you back.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: No Time To Die is startling, exotically self-aware, funny and confident, and perhaps most of all it is big: big action, big laughs, big stunts...
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Put your fears to rest, because Daniel Craig and Cary Joji Fukunaga make their shot count...
reviews.author: Mike Reyes

reviews.text: Fukunaga stages some fine chases, explosions, stunts, and the big hour long finale... but there is as much emphasis on the human beings here, their conflicts and complications and complexities as there is on the fast moving thrills.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Delivers all the spectacle you'd expect from a 007 movie, throws a few surprises in along the way and proves to be an entertaining, affecting and bold finale for Daniel Craig.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

synopsis: In No Time To Die, Bond has left active service and is enjoying a tranquil life in Jamaica. His peace is short-lived when his old friend Felix Leiter from the CIA turns up asking for help. The mission to rescue a kidnapped scientist turns out to be far more treacherous than expected, leading Bond onto the trail of a mysterious villain armed with dangerous new technology.
